claims.claim: TULIP-1's prespecified primary endpoint was SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules.
The primary analysis missed the endpoint: mean difference -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8), p=0.412, favoring neither group convincingly.
The curated record states TULIP-1 missed SRI-4, a composite lupus response measure.

claims.claim: Post-hoc SRI-4 analyses with revised restricted medication rules at Week 52 also failed: mean difference 3.9 (95% CI -6.3 to 14.1), p=0.455 for OG001 vs OG002.
Post-hoc SRI-4 at Week 24 with revised rules also failed: mean difference 3.3 (95% CI -6.7 to 13.4), p=0.515.
Post-hoc BICLA at Week 52 with revised rules appeared favorable: mean difference 16.4 (95% CI 6.7 to 26.2), p not reported.
Prespecified BICLA at Week 52 with original rules showed mean difference 10.1 (95% CI 0.6 to 19.7), p not reported.
After failure, AstraZeneca pivoted to BICLA for TULIP-2 because evaluation showed a more favorable response using BICLA, an alternative measure already collected in the program.

claims.claim: TULIP-1's prespecified primary endpoint was SRI-4 at Week 52 under original restricted medication rules; the anifrolumab vs placebo mean difference was -4.2 (95% CI -14.2 to 5.8, p=0.412), so it missed the primary endpoint.

Post-hoc analyses with revised restricted medication rules did not rescue SRI-4 at Week 52 (mean difference 3.9, 95% CI -6.3 to 14.1, p=0.455) or at Week 24 (mean difference 3.3, 95% CI -6.7 to 13.4, p=0.515).

A post-hoc BICLA analysis with revised restricted medication rules at Week 52 showed a more favorable response (mean difference 16.4, 95% CI 6.7 to 26.2), supporting BICLA as an alternative endpoint already collected in the program.

After TULIP-1 failed SRI-4, AstraZeneca chose BICLA for TULIP-2; TULIP-2 succeeded and Saphnelo received US approval in 2021, confirming the revised endpoint in another trial rather than retroactively converting TULIP-1 into a success.
